- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–2% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates further decline; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment day.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to counteract lag.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model lags in adjusting; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- In 30-day horizon, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture continuation; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to reflect momentum carryover.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is near recent high, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid peak overhang.
